concerns.text: T023a and T023b define components (loss function, cross-term) but T023 (the consumer task) is listed AFTER them in the same phase. However, T023 depends on T023a/T023b. The ordering is technically correct (producer before consumer), BUT T023 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) while it explicitly depends on T023a and T023b. A task cannot be parallel-safe if it has hard dependencies on other tasks in the same phase that must complete first. This violates the [P] correctness rule.

T024a, T024b, T024c, T024d, T025, T025b, T025c are all marked [P] (parallel-safe) but they all depend on T023 (Loss function implementation). T023 is a single task. If T023 is not completed, none of these can run. Furthermore, T024b depends on T072 (runtime monitor), and T024d depends on T073. These tasks are grouped as [P] but have distinct, non-parallelizable dependencies on foundational tasks that must be completed first. The [P] tag is misleading here as they cannot run in parallel with each other until T023, T072, and T073 are done, and even then, they share a common dependency chain.

T025b depends on T025, which depends on T023b. T025b is marked [P]. However, T025b reads `data/results/cross_term_log.json` produced by T025. T025 writes this file. T025b cannot run until T025 completes. The [P] tag on T025b is incorrect as it has a strict sequential dependency on T025.

T031 depends on T030b (Bootstrap). T030b is marked [P]. T031 is NOT marked [P]. This is correct. However, T031 also depends on T012 and T024c. T012 is in Phase 3, T024c is in Phase 4. The dependency chain is clear. BUT, T032 depends on T031. T032 is NOT marked [P]. This is correct. The issue is T029a depends on T072. T072 is in Phase 8. This creates a circular or out-of-order dependency if Phase 5 tasks are expected to run before Phase 8. T029a (Phase 5) depends on T072 (Phase 8). This is a hard ordering violation: a consumer (T029a) is placed before its producer (T072).

T029b (Driver) is listed in Phase 5. It orchestrates the multi-seed loop. It depends on T012 (Baseline) and T024c (Quantum). T012 is Phase 3, T024c is Phase 4. This is fine. However, T029b is marked [P]. It cannot run in parallel with T012 or T024c. The [P] tag is incorrect.

T074-T087 all depend on T071 (research.md skeleton). T071 is in Phase 7A. T074-T087 are in Phase 7B. This is correct. However, T074-T087 are all marked [P]. They can run in parallel with each other, but they all depend on T071. This is acceptable for [P] within the group, provided T071 is done. BUT, T074-T087 also depend on results from Phase 3, 4, 5, 6 (T012, T024c, T031, T037). The tasks are listed in Phase 7, which is after Phase 6. This is correct. The [P] tag is valid for the group relative to each other, but the dependency on T071 must be respected.

T072 (Full Run Wrapper) is in Phase 8. It depends on T009d (runtime_monitor). T009d is in Phase 2. This is correct. However, T029a (Phase 5) depends on T072. This is a hard ordering violation: T029a (Phase 5) cannot run before T072 (Phase 8). The dependency graph is broken.

T094 (Code) and T100 (Code) create new code artifacts. T094 depends on T093 (Doc). T100 depends on T098/T099 (Doc). These are in Phase 9. T094 and T100 are marked [P]. They can run in parallel with other Phase 9 tasks, but they depend on specific Doc tasks. This is acceptable. However, T094 and T100 are not traced to any FR/SC in the spec. While this is a scope issue, the ordering is fine. The main issue is the [P] tag on tasks that have dependencies on other Phase 9 tasks. If T093 is not done, T094 cannot run. The [P] tag implies no dependencies, which is false.

T008 is marked [X] [Foundational] [DEPRECATED]. It should be removed or clearly marked as skipped to avoid confusion in the dependency graph. The [X] checkmark implies it is done, but the text says DEPRECATED. This is a minor clarity issue.

T023 is marked [Foundational] but it is in Phase 4 (User Story 2). Foundational tasks should be in Phase 2. This is a labeling inconsistency, though the dependency order (T023 before T024a) is correct. The [Foundational] tag is misleading in Phase 4.
